description: Reaches the LOCAL estate - http and ws on localhost or a private LAN address, ANY port - through the Tauri http and websocket plugins. It is OPT-IN: tauri.conf.json names only 'default', and src-tauri/tauri.local.conf.json (or the TAURI_CONFIG the iOS local-device build sets) is the only thing that adds this capability, so no release build can compile it. The port wildcards are mandatory, not decoration: an EMPTY port in a URLPattern means the protocol's DEFAULT port, so 'http://**' matches port 80 and nothing else - which is why the local estate on :8081 was refused while 'https://**' worked, 443 being https's default. The LAN patterns exist for the iPhone, which has no `adb reverse` and reaches the workstation by its address on the Wi-Fi; they are deliberately loose (10.*, 192.168.*) because only a build made by hand for a bench can carry them.
